## Purpose

Hooks that fan out one query per registered project do not hand back raw `UseQueryResult`s — they expose a purpose-built row view. An exported `interface <Feature>Row` carries exactly four things: the identity (`project: ProjectEntry` or `path: string`), the possibly-undefined payload, `isLoading: boolean`, and `error: unknown`. The hook reads the project list from `useProjectsStore`, builds `useQueries` with `queryKey: ["<prefix>", p.path]` so cache identity follows the project rather than the array index, then maps the results back into a collection aligned 1:1 with `projects` (an array in `useProjectDetections`, a `Record<path, Row>` in `useArtifactDrift`) — the header comment in `useProjectDetections.ts` calls this the dashboard's canonical fan-out convention precisely so callers never re-zip by position. Every access is defensive and the queries set `retry: false`, because a project that is not a Mustard repo is an expected miss: the payload collapses to undefined and the sidebar simply skips the badge.

## Convention

- Declared and exported inside the fan-out hook's own file under `apps/dashboard/src/hooks/`, extension `.ts`; 2 hooks use this shape today.
- Interface name is `<Feature>Row`; the payload member is named after the DTO it holds (`detection`, `report`), not `data`.
- `staleTime` reflects the real cadence of the underlying work (30s for an installation stat, 60s for drift), with a comment justifying it.

## How to apply

When a new surface needs per-project data, export a `<Feature>Row` interface with the identity, payload, `isLoading` and `error` members, key each query by `p.path`, and return the aligned array or record — do not return the `useQueries` result directly and do not index queries by array position outside the mapping step. Keep the query function pointing at a wrapper from `@/lib/projects` (or the matching lib module); the hook itself never calls `invoke()`. Leave the payload optional so a failing project degrades to a skipped badge instead of an error state, and let the general hook conventions (query key prefix registered in `lib/watcher.ts`, explicit `staleTime`) apply unchanged.

## Examples

- Ref: `apps/dashboard/src/hooks/useProjectDetections.ts` — `ProjectDetectionRow[]` aligned 1:1 with the store's projects.
- Ref: `apps/dashboard/src/hooks/useArtifactDrift.ts` — `Record<string, ArtifactDriftRow>` keyed by path, `retry: false`, commented staleTime.
